note: Sentences that interpret the full Earth run, read by scripts/fill_submission.py. They apply only to a run with this spec digest. Aggregates only: no prompt or answer text belongs here.

sentences.GAP_TABLE_SETUP_SENTENCE: Aya Expanse 8B and Qwen3-8B judged every answer, on 170 to 178 harmful prompts per language.
sentences.GAP_FAILURE_TYPE_SENTENCE: Almost none of the Javanese gap is harmful content. With the preamble, Earth's 17 fewer safe answers there are 10 more broken answers and 7 more that the judges split on, and both judges called just 1 of 176 answers unsafe for each model.
sentences.GAP_SAFE_ANY_SENTENCE: If either judge's `safe` were enough, and broken answers still didn't count, Javanese with the preamble would read 96.0% for Global and 90.3% for Earth, a gap of 5.7 points.
sentences.GAP_PROMPTS_SENTENCE: We used 170 to 178 harmful prompts per language. Bengali, Javanese, Korean, Swahili and Thai use MultiJail alone, Arabic has 46 from MultiJail and 124 from Aya red-teaming, and English has 37 from MultiJail, 114 from Aya red-teaming and 27 XSTest contrast prompts.
sentences.BLIND_AUDIT_SENTENCE: Readers labelled 240 random answers from Global and Earth in each of Thai and Javanese, on 60 prompts in each preamble condition, without seeing the judges' labels or which model wrote them. In Thai, the target language, they found no gap: with the preamble, 88.3% of Global's answers were safe and 90.0% of Earth's (-1.7 points, 95% CI -10.0 to 6.7), and without it 91.7% and 93.3%. They agreed with 94% to 97% of the judges' safe calls there, and each model had 2 to 4 unsafe answers in 60. In Javanese, where the gap was confirmed, they found 80.0% of Global's answers safe with the preamble and 60.0% of Earth's, a gap of 20.0 points (95% CI 8.3 to 31.7). A second read of those 120 answers matched on 94% of labels and found a gap of 13.3 points (3.3 to 25.0). Both reads put the Javanese gap in invalid answers: Earth had 1 unsafe answer of 60 in each read, and Global had 2 and 3. An English control found no gap (3.3 points, p = 0.63), with 1 of 60 invalid for each model. All the readers are the same model, so their agreement doesn't show that they are right.
sentences.JUDGE_LIMIT_SENTENCE: In Javanese the judges often passed broken text: readers found 34 of the 207 answers the judges called safe to be invalid, and 6 to be unsafe, so the judges understate the drop in usable answers. In Thai they held up better: readers agreed with 94% to 97% of the answers the judges called safe.
sentences.FIRE_COMPARISON_SENTENCE: On the judges' numbers, Fire also falls below Global in Javanese, by 10.8 points with the preamble and 6.8 without, mostly through broken answers, and it stays within 0.6 points in Bengali. A blind read of 60 of its Javanese answers was too small to settle this: 75.0% safe against Global's 80.0%, a gap of 5.0 points (95% CI -3.3 to 13.3).
sentences.WATER_CONTROL_SENTENCE: Water shows no Javanese gap on the judges' numbers (2.3 and -0.6 points) or in a blind read (3.3 points, 95% CI -5.0 to 11.7). It falls 9.7 and 10.2 points in Bengali on the judges' numbers, but most of that is answers the judges split on, and a partial blind read found 2.9 points on 34 pairs. So the data doesn't settle whether the gap follows the region. These comparisons sit outside the 14 tests, and Fire and Water were read in a separate batch from Global and Earth.
sentences.THESIS_VERDICT_GAP_SENTENCE: The first half of the thesis did not hold as written. The one confirmed gap is in Javanese, outside Earth's region, while in Arabic and Swahili, the languages Earth targets, Earth stays within 1.2 points of Global. It isn't a weakening of refusals either: both models fully refused 33.0% of Javanese harmful prompts with the preamble, though the judges' refusal labels fall below our agreement floor in Javanese, so that figure is rough. Earth's extra failures are broken answers.
sentences.SPEC_LATER_AMENDMENTS_SENTENCE: Two amendments followed the freeze, after the baseline and before any repair result. They added further blind reads as description and changed no test, gate or stage.
sentences.GAP_LOCATION_SENTENCE: Javanese is outside Earth's region. Bengali, Thai and Korean, also outside it, show gaps of 4.5 to 8.5 points with the preamble that miss the corrected bar, while in Arabic and Swahili, the two languages in Earth's region, Earth stays within 1.2 points of Global in both conditions.
sentences.OTHER_MODELS_LIMIT_SENTENCE: We tested Tiny Aya alone. Fire and Water give comparisons on the same prompts, but they share Earth's base model and training recipe, so none of this shows how other model families behave.
sentences.REPAIR_BLIND_READ_SENTENCE: Readers also labelled 120 of the selected arm's answers in each of Thai and Javanese, blind, on the same prompts as the reads above (60 in each preamble condition). In Thai they saw no change from Earth: with the preamble, 93.3% of its answers were safe against Earth's 90.0% and Global's 88.3%, and without it 88.3% against 93.3% and 91.7% (p = 0.63 and 0.25 against Earth). In Javanese, where Earth's lost safe answers were mostly broken ones, the repair left them broken: 63.3% of its answers were safe with the preamble (Earth 60.0%, Global 80.0%) and 71.7% without it (Earth 75.0%, Global 88.3%), 16.7 points below Global in both conditions (95% CI 6.7 to 28.3 with the preamble, 6.7 to 26.7 without), and 35% and 28% of its answers were invalid. Unsafe answers stayed rare: 2 of 60 in each Thai condition, and 1 and 0 in Javanese. The judges, scoring the same answers, agree in Thai: they called 88.3% and 90.0% of them safe, and readers agreed with 96% and 98% of those calls. In Javanese they again passed broken text, calling 80.0% and 88.3% safe, of which readers agreed with only 71% and 79%. These readers worked in a separate batch from the earlier reads, so the comparisons with Earth and Global also carry differences between readers.
sentences.FAILED_CONDITION: all three, with the preamble: it closed 10% of the Thai gap against the 50% required, refused 3 more of 142 benign Thai prompts (2.1 points, against a cap of 2), and got 5 more of 400 Swahili capability questions wrong (1.25 points, against a cap of 1). Merge-back, the same edit applied to the whole model, came nearest: it closed 90% of the gap but also missed on over-refusal and capability
sentences.NO_ARM_PASSED_SENTENCE: Thai's gap was never confirmed (5.7 points with the preamble, 95% CI 1.7 to 10.2, short of the corrected bar), so under Amendment 17 every repair result here is exploratory, and no arm could have counted as a success. On the numbers alone, with the preamble: ReSta closed 30% of the gap and missed on over-refusal (Thai +7.0 points) and capability (Korean −3.0); Circuit closed none of it (the gap widened by a tenth) and missed on over-refusal (Javanese +3.4); Merge-back closed 90% and missed on over-refusal (Arabic +2.6) and capability (Arabic and Indonesian −1.5); Circuit merge closed 10% and missed all three; Steering closed 30% and missed on over-refusal (Thai +3.5), though it was the only arm inside the capability bar in both conditions. The over-refusal and capability bars come to 3 benign prompts and 4 test questions per language, and the random-layer controls crossed them too, so those two gates sit near the noise of our measures. The gap gate does not: only Merge-back and one random-layer control cleared it.
sentences.PREAMBLE_FINDING_SENTENCE: Without the preamble, Earth's Thai gap is only 2.3 points, 4 prompts of 176, and too small to measure, so the fractions closed there are noise: Merge-back closed all of it, Circuit merge none, and all three random-layer controls ended below Earth. In this condition Circuit merge stays inside the capability bar (its largest drop is 0.5 points, in Swahili) but still misses on over-refusal (English +2.6).
sentences.LOCALISATION_FINDING_SENTENCE: Confining the edit to the circuit made it a quarter to a third the size and kept up to 1.5 points more capability, but it did not make the model safer. With the preamble, Circuit merge gave 4.5 points fewer safe Thai answers than whole-model Merge-back (95% CI −9.1 to 0.0), and 2.3 fewer without it (−5.7 to 1.1). Against the same edit on random layers it differed by −2.8 to +2.8 points across the three seeds and two conditions, and every interval spans zero. One pattern held in all six random-layer comparisons: the circuit's layers gave 2.8 to 5.1 points more full refusals in Thai, though only two of those intervals exclude zero, before any correction. On this evidence, the circuit map finds layers where an edit nudges refusals a little more than chance, not layers that fix the answers Earth gets wrong.
sentences.THESIS_VERDICT_REPAIR_SENTENCE: The second half did not hold either. No repair met all three conditions at full precision, so none could hold at 4-bit, and the arm placed with CircuitKIT's map did no better on Thai safety than the same edit on randomly chosen layers.
sentences.KAPPA_LOCAL_VS_ROUTER: 0.79 to 1.00 per language on refusal labels (median 0.93). The sample was 1,680 held-out answers from Global, Earth and the selected repair, 20 from every language, harmful or benign, and preamble cell. Bengali, Javanese and Swahili were lowest.
